parsed.explanation: Combined regime, national passport and entry rules plus division facility and ID rules. Documented exposures: national passports show birth sex, X markers are no longer issued, and passports have been confiscated or blocked, stranding some travellers. Entry officers may refuse cases with discrepancies, and a lifetime fraud ineligibility is possible. Immigration and national custody harms are documented, including forced labour, beatings, and sexual abuse. The division adds a birth-sex facility designation for schools and colleges with no penalty or documented enforcement, and marker rules are tightening (August 2026 announcement). Mitigations are real but partial: marriage recognition, national employment protection, and 33 local ordinances. Enforcement of the protections is not documented for visitors. Score sits in the elevated band.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports issued as M or F by birth sex; X markers no longer issued; discrepancies trigger refusal and document requests. Passports confiscated or blocked, with stranding reported. Possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for suspected wilful misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry. Litigation ongoing; Supreme Court allowed restrictions to take effect.
entry_documents.interaction: National passport regime governs all entry; division ID rules (August 2026 marker restriction) add a second document mismatch at state level.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. Corrections policies from 2026 include hair cutting and hormone removal. Corrections bureau stopped reporting transgender prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: National custody regime applies to any traveller detained; the division's facility rule has no custody provision.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division facility law requires birth-certificate-based designation in all K-12 schools, colleges and universities, public and private, including overnight accommodation. Applies to students and visitors in those settings. Nationwide facility bans exist in other states; the division's trespass-type arrest is documented elsewhere and its link to this division is unclear.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single-occupancy controlled-use restrooms are exempt. No criminal penalty or enforcement mechanism in the division statute.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Institutional refusal by schools is the realistic channel; the national regime does not add a penalty here, but the designation duty is universal for covered institutions.

care_services.exposure: National subpoenas for minors' hospital records; proposed national rules to bar public reimbursement for under-18 care. Division care ban for under-18s was re-enjoined in March 2025; current status unresolved.
care_services.protection: Adult care rules proposed in 2024 were withdrawn and are not in force.
care_services.interaction: Minor care access depends on unresolved litigation at both levels; adult visitors face no documented division-level care restriction.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as targets for neutralisation; cash reward scheme. Executive orders direct investigation of schools for 'gender ideology'. Division law requires school staff to disclose LGBTQ students to parents. Trans candidates were disqualified.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism powers stated not to target people who simply disagree.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat framing and division disclosure duty operate on schools and civic life; visitors face indirect exposure.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor travellers face the school designation duty, the staff disclosure duty, and minor care bans under litigation. Guardians face possible hospital records subpoenas and proposed reimbursement limits.
minors_guardians.protection: Care and sports bans are contested; the sports and care bill's operative status is unverified.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor enrolled in a covered school meets the facility rule and the disclosure duty, so exposure reaches the guardian through the school.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific street violence rate documented in the dossier. National hate-crime statute exists, but only 23 states cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute applies nationally; 33 local ordinances bar gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local ordinances are patchy and do not cover all visitor settings; national hate-crime recourse is available but enforcement is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport litigation, county refusals of birth-certificate corrections, and the August 2026 marker rule (announcement only) are unresolved. Enforcement of the facility law is undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Birth-certificate corrections permitted since 2021 in principle; marriage recognised for same-sex couples; state employment executive order since 2018; national employment law applies.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are partial and slow; visitors cannot rely on them for document or custody exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier. Both involve discretionary entry refusal and exclusion without imprisonment. This case adds a lifetime fraud ground and documented stranding, but lacks a universal visitor register and the custody abuse record, so it is comparable overall.

Similar tier. Both involve durable registration-style exposure and discretionary enforcement. This case has documented immigration custody abuse and national threat framing, which are heavier, so it sits slightly lower.

Lower. The anchor has documented housing by birth sex with assaults and arrests for presentation in state buildings. Here the division's facility rule has no penalty or documented enforcement, and national custody harm is documented but not tied to routine street arrests, so this case sits higher.

parsed.synthesis: The national passport regime is a universal, documented exposure at every entry, and discrepancies can trigger refusal, stranding, or lifetime fraud ineligibility. Documented custody harms in immigration and national corrections raise severity. The division's facility rule reaches schools and colleges for students and any visitor in those settings but carries no penalty and no documented case. Division marker tightening and minor care litigation remain unresolved. Protections are real but limited to employment, local ordinances, and marriage, and no operative visitor-facing remedy is documented. The combined regime sits in the elevated band.
